0|7cbe5dca399a50ce8aa74314b1d276e2fb904e1b|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"USB: add API for userspace drivers to ""claim"" ports
This patch (as1258) implements a feature that users have been asking
for: It gives programs the ability to ""claim"" a port on a hub
new usbfs ioctl.  A device plugged into a ""claimed"" port will not be
touched by the kernel beyond the immediate necessities of
initialization and enumeration.
In particular
column2: when a device is plugged into a ""claimed"" port

column1: kernel will not select and install a configuration.  And when a config
is installed by usbfs or sysfs
column2: the kernel will not probe any drivers

column1: for any of the interfaces.  (However the kernel will fetch various
string descriptors during enumeration.  One could argue that this
isn't really necessary
column2: but the strings are exported in sysfs.)

column1: The patch does not guarantee exclusive access to these devices; it is
still possible for more than one program to open the device file
concurrently.  Programs are responsible for coordinating access among
themselves.
A demonstration program showing how to use the new interface can be
found in an attachment to
http://marc.info/?l=linux-usb&m=124345857431452&w=2
The patch also makes a small simplification to the hub driver
replacing a bunch of more-or-less useless variants of ""out of memory""
with a single message.
